# Continuous integration

- `workflows/ci.yml` runs on pull requests, pushes to `master` and manual dispatch (no duplicate push runs for PR branches). Checks cover frontend formatting/types/tests, Go race tests and `make lint` (golangci-lint version pinned in Makefile, host and Windows targets; `.tools` is cached by Makefile/go.mod hash; the linter is built with throwaway caches, and "Windows build" keys its setup-go cache by go.sum + Makefile so the Wails CLI build does not land in the checks cache. Caches are immutable per key: after changing what jobs build, delete stale `setup-go-*` entries so they are re-saved). Four parallel jobs, split by duration rather than language: "Go tests" (Linux, `go test -race` and vet only), "Lint and frontend checks" (Linux; needs both Go for bindings/linting and Vite+), "Windows tests" (only native Go tests on the Windows runner, no frontend toolchain) and "Windows build" (Linux cross-build via `make vet build`, then artifact upload). All four job names are required status checks on `master`; renaming a job requires updating branch protection first.
- "Go tests" also runs `make stt-worker-test` (speech worker unit tests) through `astral-sh/setup-uv` pinned by SHA; uv fetches the pinned Python 3.12/numpy/websockets/soxr, never torch or the model.
- Use the official setup-vp action with working-directory frontend. It resolves the pinned Vite+ catalog and manages Node/pnpm. Install with --frozen-lockfile; do not introduce npm/yarn installs or manually regenerate the lockfile in CI.
- Pin third-party action references to commit SHAs and keep version comments accurate. Use read-only contents permission, timeouts and cancellation of superseded runs. No secrets, real Codex requests or pull_request_target execution.
- Build through Makefile targets so CI and local `make check` share the Wails CLI version and flags. Generate bindings natively before compiling frontend; frontend output must exist before vet/build of the root application. Keep the Windows runner for behavior that needs native Windows; it is slower and costs more minutes.
- Upload only `build/bin/Solveo.exe` and `SHA256SUMS.txt`, with finite retention. Never upload solveo-data, profiles or the entire workspace. Artifacts are available for PR review independently of the other jobs; publication requires all four checks to pass.
- Only a push to `master` publishes `build-<run_number>` through the release job with `contents: write`; PR/manual runs cannot publish. Download the exact build artifact by ID, verify its checksum and publish without rebuilding. Keep master runs uncancelled and release jobs serialized; the script rechecks the master head because concurrency ordering is not guaranteed. Superseded commits skip publication. Reruns finish a matching draft or preserve an already published release and its assets. Never overwrite published assets. `.github/scripts/publish-release.sh` owns these rules; validate it with fake `gh`, without real publication.
- These are unsigned build releases, not semantic versions or evidence of recorder/UI acceptance. Use `docs/windows-acceptance.md` for native runtime verification.
- Validate workflow syntax with actionlint and run the relevant local build/check commands. Keep CI maintenance details here rather than in the product README.
